title: Non-destructive Enzymatic DNA Extraction from Arthropod Specimens
author: Daubian Santos
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.kkqcuvw
materials: Extract DNA from digestion buffer collected after 16 hours of specimen incubation with the employment of a PCR fragment purification kit (Qiagen, Thermo Scientific, Promega, BioRad), following manufacturer instructions, and dissolve DNA in 30uL

steps.title: Prepare tube and add digestion buffer
steps.instruction: Place the insect in a 1.5 mL sterile tube and add enough digestion buffer to fully submerge it (e.g., 200 µL for Aedes specimens). The buffer should contain 200 mM Tris‑HCl, 250 mM NaCl, 25 mM EDTA, 0.5 % de‑SDS, and 400 µg/mL Proteinase K, adding the Proteinase K at this moment to start digestion.

steps.title: Incubate for enzymatic digestion
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube at 56 °C for 16 hours.

steps.title: Recover buffer and assess clarification
steps.instruction: Using a micropipette, collect the digestion buffer and transfer it to a new sterile tube. Examine the specimen under a stereomicroscope to verify tissue clarification.

substeps.instruction: If clarification is insufficient, add fresh digestion buffer to the specimen and incubate again at 56 °C until the desired clarity for morphological studies is achieved.
Discard the used digestion buffer after the final clarification check.

steps.title: Preserve specimen post‑extraction
steps.instruction: Cover the cleared specimen with 80 % ethanol and store it at ambient temperature.
